items.title: Reasoning Part 1
items.description: A model's thinking, folded away behind a disclosure so it never competes with the answer. The trigger shimmers while tokens are still arriving and settles once the step closes. Takes an AI SDK reasoning part.

items.name: text-part-1
items.title: Text Part 1
items.description: A message's text. An answer is parsed as markdown by Streamdown, which copes with the half-finished syntax a stream produces and gives code blocks their own header and controls. A question is rendered literally, because its asterisks are asterisks. Takes an AI SDK text part.
items.docs: Add `import "streamdown/styles.css"` to your root layout. It cannot be added for you, and without it code blocks render without their chrome. The two `@source` lines assume your stylesheet sits one folder deep, as `app/globals.css` does; add a `../` for each extra level if yours is deeper.

items.name: tool-part-1
items.title: Tool Part 1
items.description: One tool call, through all four of its states: running, done, failed and refused. A denied call reads differently from one that simply errored, and expanding either prints what went in or came back, as a code block you can copy in one click. Takes an AI SDK tool part, whichever tool it is.

items.name: web-search-part-1
items.title: Web Search Part 1
items.description: The line saying a search happened: objective and a spinner while it runs, a warning when it fails. What it found is not rendered here, because the citations under the answer already carry it; without this row the slowest step of a turn happens in silence.

items.name: questionnaire-part-1
items.title: Questionnaire Part 1
items.description: The agent asking before it commits to expensive work: a multi-step form rendered inside the message, with choices, multi-select, a freeform field, validation and keyboard shortcuts. A tool rather than a data part, so the answers return as that tool call's output and survive a reload. Answered, it collapses to a summary of what was chosen.
items.docs: The renderer owns the input and output contracts (`QuestionnaireData`, `QuestionnaireAnswers`); your route's tool definition carries the matching JSON schema, registered without `execute` so the turn stalls at `input-available` for the browser to answer. Pass `onAnswer` from the chat that owns `useChat` and return the answers through `addToolOutput`.

items.name: sources-part-1
items.title: Sources Part 1
items.description: The citation list under an answer, collapsed to a count until asked for. Citations reach a chat by two different routes, streamed by the provider or buried inside a search tool's output, and this gathers both into one list with the duplicates dropped.

The composition balances authority and social density, making it effective when you want a strong narrative supported by visible team adoption rather than a single spokesperson.

items.name: testimonials-9
items.title: Testimonial 9 – Multi-segment case cards
items.description: A testimonial layout built around small, self-contained story cards, each representing a different team or use case. The grid creates quick scanability while still allowing depth per card, making it well suited to showcasing breadth of adoption across industries rather than a single standout quote.

items.name: testimonials-10
items.title: Testimonial 10 – Dense quote grid
items.description: A compact testimonial layout that surfaces many short quotes at once using a uniform card grid. Designed for volume and credibility, it emphasizes breadth of feedback over individual storytelling, making it effective for scanning, comparison, and reinforcing widespread adoption.

items.name: testimonials-11
items.title: Testimonial 11 – Editorial quote grid
items.description: A structured testimonial layout that combines a clear section header with a multi-column grid of short quotes. It balances scannability and depth by presenting many voices at once, using consistent cards and subtle hierarchy to reinforce trust without relying on a single standout story.

items.name: testimonials-12
items.title: Testimonial 12 – Featured quote with supporting cards
items.description: A hybrid testimonial layout that anchors the section with a single, prominent featured quote and portrait, supported by smaller secondary quotes beneath. It creates a clear hierarchy: one strong endorsement to lead, with additional voices adding breadth and credibility without competing for attention.

items.name: testimonials-13
items.title: Testimonial 13 – Single featured testimonial with inline pagination
items.description: A clean, focused testimonial layout built around one primary quote and portrait, with minimal controls to step through additional testimonials. Strong visual emphasis on the individual builds trust and authority, while inline pagination keeps the layout compact and distraction-free.

items.name: testimonials-14
items.title: Testimonial 14 – Dual quote carousel with ratings
items.description: A two-up testimonial layout showing parallel quotes with star ratings, names, and roles. Uses carousel controls to rotate content while keeping density low. Works well when you want social proof without large imagery and want to highlight consistency across multiple voices. Includes pagination.

items.name: testimonials-15
items.title: Testimonial 15 – Image-led quote cards
items.description: A two-card layout that pairs large, contextual photos with short quotes and author details. Feels more human and story-driven than avatar cards. Best when you want atmosphere and team presence to do some of the credibility work, not just the text.

items.name: testimonials-16
items.title: Testimonial 16 – Single hero testimonial
items.description: A focused, one-voice layout with a large contextual image and a single quote. Very clear hierarchy. Works best when you have one strong story you want people to actually read, not skim. Good for mid-page trust reinforcement rather than a dense social proof wall.

items.name: testimonials-17
items.title: Testimonial 17 – Testimonial with supporting metrics
items.description: This one blends a strong personal quote with credibility stats. The testimonial does the emotional work, while the numbers add reassurance without overwhelming it. Best used near conversion points where people want proof and scale, not just praise.

items.name: testimonials-18
items.title: Testimonial 18 – Multi-quote card carousel
items.description: This pattern breaks one customer into multiple short quotes, each paired with a different visual. It’s good for scanning and variety, but weaker on trust unless the context is clear. Works best as supporting social proof rather than a primary testimonial.

items.name: testimonials-19
items.title: Testimonial 19 – Image carousel with quote overlays
items.description: A horizontally scrolling set of image-led cards, each using a full-bleed photo with a subtle gradient overlay to anchor short quotes and author details. pagination controls sit inline, reinforcing the carousel behavior without dominating the layout. On smaller screens, the design collapses into a single-card vertical rail for focused browsing. Works well when you want visual consistency, motion, and repeatable social proof without turning the section into a dense grid.

items.name: testimonials-20
items.title: Testimonial 20 – Split heading and featured quote
items.description: A minimal, two-column layout that separates context from content. The left side anchors the section with a static heading and short intro, while the right side highlights a single, prominent quote with author details and inline navigation. The structure creates a strong reading flow and keeps focus on one testimonial at a time. On smaller screens, it stacks into a compact, single-column carousel for clarity and continuity.

items.name: testimonials-21
items.title: Testimonial 21 – Auto-scrolling quote cards
items.description: A horizontally auto-scrolling row of compact testimonial cards paired with a centered section header. Cards move continuously to showcase multiple quotes without user input, creating motion and density while keeping each card lightweight and readable. Designed to surface social proof at scale, with a smooth transition to a single-card carousel on smaller screens to maintain focus and pacing.

items.name: testimonials-22
items.title: Testimonial 22 – Auto-scrolling stacked columns
items.description: A multi-column testimonial layout where cards are arranged in vertical stacks that auto-scroll in opposing or offset directions. This creates a dense, editorial-style wall of social proof with constant motion, while preserving clear card boundaries and scanability. Works well for showcasing many short testimonials at once, with a simplified single-column experience on smaller screens to keep it readable.

items.name: testimonials-23
items.title: Testimonial 23 – Masonry quote cards
items.description: A three-column masonry layout with compact quote cards beneath a centered section heading. Varied card heights accommodate different quote lengths, while avatars, names, roles and verification badges provide clear attribution. The arrangement makes multiple customer voices easy to scan, working well when you want a broad collection of short endorsements without giving one testimonial priority.

items.name: top-navigation-1
items.title: Top Navigation 1 – Left-aligned dropdown navigation
items.description: A classic left-aligned top navigation with horizontal links and inline dropdown menus for larger screens. Primary actions are grouped on the right for clear visual separation. On smaller screens, the layout collapses into a full-height mobile menu with expandable sections, preserving hierarchy while keeping the interaction simple and familiar.

items.name: top-navigation-2
items.title: Top Navigation 2 – Centered primary navigation
items.description: A center-aligned top navigation that places the primary links in the middle of the header, creating a more balanced, symmetrical layout. Dropdown menus open directly beneath each item on larger screens, while actions remain grouped to the right. On smaller screens, the navigation collapses into a vertical, full-height menu with expandable sections, keeping the structure clear while shifting focus to touch-friendly interaction.

items.name: top-navigation-3
items.title: Top Navigation 3 – Compact bar with progressive disclosure
items.description: A compact top navigation that keeps the large-screen layout minimal and low-profile, with primary links arranged in a single horizontal bar. Dropdowns reveal richer, icon-led menus only when needed, keeping visual noise down by default. On smaller screens, the same structure expands into a stacked, panel-style menu with nested sections, preserving hierarchy while shifting emphasis to vertical scanning and tap targets.

items.name: top-navigation-4
items.title: Top Navigation 4 – Centered pill navigation with dropdown menu
items.description: A centered top navigation where primary links sit inside a pill-style container, creating a strong visual anchor across large screens. Dropdown menus open from the center group to reveal secondary links in a compact panel. On small screens, the layout collapses into a full-height drawer with stacked links and clear primary actions, maintaining the same information structure while prioritizing tap comfort and readability.

items.name: top-navigation-5
items.title: Top Navigation 5 – Minimal center-aligned links with inline auth
items.description: A stripped-back, center-aligned top navigation that prioritizes clarity and whitespace. Primary links sit in a single horizontal row with the brand anchored to the left and a lightweight login action on the right. On small screens, the layout collapses into a simple slide-out menu with stacked links and a single secondary action, keeping the structure familiar while reducing visual noise.

items.title: 404 1 – Minimalist error page with navigation recovery actions
items.description: A clean and centered error page design for handling "Page not found" scenarios. The layout features a clear information hierarchy starting with the "404" status code, followed by a bold headline and a brief, friendly explanation. Below the text, two distinct call-to-action buttons—a primary "Back home" and a secondary "Go back" with an arrow icon—provide users with immediate paths to resume their browsing.

items.title: 404 2 – Visual 404 error page with immersive split-screen layout
items.description: A modern and emotionally engaging error page that uses a split-screen composition. The left side provides clear, left-aligned information: the "404" status code, a bold headline, a supportive description, and two navigation recovery buttons. The right side features a high-impact, artistic image that reflects the brand's aesthetic, transforming a negative technical moment into a stylish brand experience.

items.title: 404 3 – Error page with multi-channel support contact cards
items.description: A comprehensive error recovery page designed to provide immediate assistance. The top section maintains the standard 404 messaging and primary navigation buttons. Below, the layout features a horizontal grid of three informative cards, each offering a different support channel. This proactive design ensures that users who encounter a dead end can easily find a way to get help.

items.title: 404 4 – Error page with conceptual plug illustration
items.description: A creative balanced error page that uses a custom illustration to communicate a technical disconnect. The layout features a two-column split: on the left, a stylized illustration of two disconnected blue plugs; on the right, the "404" status code, a bold headline, and a friendly message explaining the potential reasons for the error. The recovery path is clearly defined by two primary action buttons.

items.title: 404 5 – Error page with immersive image and support directory
items.description: A highly functional error page that utilizes a balanced grid system. The layout is dominated on the right by a large, atmospheric image with rounded corners. The left side is divided into two clear zones: a top section containing the "404" status code, headline, and primary buttons, and a bottom section featuring a three-column support directory. This directory provides direct links for Email, Phone, and Live Chat.

items.title: 404 6 – Split-screen 404 page with high-contrast editorial visual
items.description: A modern error page that utilizes an inverted split-screen layout. A large, stylized editorial image with rounded corners is positioned on the left. The right side contains the focused messaging area, featuring the "404" status code, a bold headline, and the standard recovery buttons. This composition provides a high-end feel, turning a common navigation hurdle into a curated brand moment.

items.name: benefits-28
items.title: Benefits 28 – Three benefits acted out in animated blocks
items.description: A centered heading above three benefits, each led by a pixelated shader tile that acts out its own line on a wall of small blocks: a pass that rebuilds only what changed, a release that advances and rolls back, and columns that scale up and down to zero. Whole blocks always fit the tile, with an even margin. Tiles are coloured from the theme's chart tokens (chart-2, 4 and 5) with the destructive token for the one block that errors, or pass tone='mono' for foreground only. No pointer interaction. Best for developer and infrastructure products.

items.name: benefits-29
items.title: Benefits 29 – Split heading with four animated text-strip benefits
items.description: A two-column benefits section: a sticky heading, copy and one action on the left, and a two-by-two grid of benefits on the right. Each is topped by a 2:1 shader tile of text drawn as dashes, set inside an even margin so only whole rows and words show, that acts out its line: a hairline search pass that leaves matches lit, a phrase that lights as the answer followed by three underlined sources, results that stop at a permissions boundary, and words rewritten live. Neutral with one theme accent, or tone='mono'.

items.name: benefits-30
items.title: Benefits 30 – Three feature cards with live transcript visuals
items.description: A centered heading above three equal feature cards. Each card is a rounded panel on a soft tinted ground holding a small piece of product UI instead of an icon: a word-by-word scroller that lights the current word against a centre tick, a transcript card with inline tags that light in turn above a summary button, and a dotted globe with language badges and pulsing pins. A short title and muted description sit under each panel with no border. Animations are CSS only and stop under prefers-reduced-motion.

items.name: benefits-31
items.title: Benefits 31 – Two-by-two feature cards with large product panels
items.description: A centered heading with two actions above a two-by-two grid of feature cards with large panels. Each panel holds real UI on a soft tinted ground: a phone mock scrolling a list of delivery stops, a dotted map where a route draws itself between stops under a status card, a stack of customer notifications that arrive one by one, and an arrival card with an avatar, badge, filling progress bar and button. A title and muted description sit under each panel. Animations are CSS only and stop under prefers-reduced-motion.

items.name: footer-5
items.title: Footer 5 – Shader call-to-action panel above link columns
items.description: A footer that opens with a rounded call-to-action panel on deep blue, where large soft orbs in blue, violet and teal drift slowly round a clear centre under fine film grain, and the nearest one leans gently toward the pointer. The panel uses the theme's dark tokens in both modes and holds a centered section heading with one line of copy and the standard primary and outline buttons. Below it sit the logo, four link columns and a copyright row.

items.name: hero-11
items.title: Hero 11 – Aurora shader hero
items.description: A full-bleed centered hero over an animated WebGL aurora: curtains of theme colour rise from the bottom edge behind the headline, which reveals word by word, with two actions. The aurora follows the pointer, pauses offscreen and holds a still frame for reduced motion. Best for launch pages that want atmosphere without imagery.

items.name: hero-12
items.title: Hero 12 – Split hero with terrain map over contour lines
items.description: A full-bleed split hero over faint ink contour lines that fold slowly and fade away behind the copy. The headline reveals word by word with two actions on the left; on the right the product is a terrain map card drawn by the same contour shader, where colour is data: the ground between the lines is tinted in flat steps of the theme's chart hue, pale in the lowlands and deeper on high ground, with heavier index contours in the same hue, survey markers, a status badge and an elevation legend on the same ramp. The page stays neutral; the pointer raises the ground beneath it. Best for mapping, climate, hardware and science products.

items.name: hero-13
items.title: Hero 13 – Split API hero with fluted-glass shader
items.description: A split developer hero: a two-tone headline that reveals word by word, copy, a primary button and a docs link on the left, with a two-column endpoint list along the bottom. The right half is a tall animated fluted-glass shader panel with a terminal card showing a sample request. Best for API and developer-platform landing pages.

items.name: hero-14
items.title: Hero 14 – Split product hero with grainy mesh-gradient shader
items.description: A split hero that leads with the visual: a tall animated mesh-gradient shader panel on the left, airbrushed into stipple with film grain and soft paper creases, holds a portrait token card with the selected colour shown large above a list of five tokens from the panel's own palette. The two-tone headline, copy and one primary action sit at the bottom right. The panel moves below the copy on mobile. Best for design tools and product-led launches.

items.name: hero-15
items.title: Hero 15 – Radiance hero with roadmap card
items.description: A full-bleed hero lit by a grainy radiance shader: a luminous sheet of colour falls from the top right, folding slowly, and leaves the bottom-left corner clear for the two-line headline, copy and two actions. A roadmap card with owners, progress bars and a status badge floats on the light at the right, and moves above the copy on mobile. Best for planning, productivity and SaaS launches.

items.name: hero-16
items.title: Hero 16 – Glass panes hero with display headline
items.description: A full-bleed hero behind tall panes of glass, each shifting a slow gradient in clean steps of one blue. The pointer is a lamp behind the glass: every pane shows it at its own height and the panes nearest it slide into line. A two-line display headline anchors the bottom left with copy and two actions at the bottom right, and a staged-rollout card floats top right. Pale sky blues in light mode, deep navy in dark mode.

items.name: hero-17
items.title: Hero 17 – Centered hero with search card over a halo
items.description: A calm full-bleed centered hero over an arc of light, like dawn seen from orbit, with a living atmosphere: haze drifts along the arc, the glow swells and thins in slow waves and its colour shifts, the camera sways a few pixels and, in dark mode, far stars twinkle. Fine film grain, no pointer interaction, and a still frame for reduced motion. The headline, copy and two actions sit above a search card with a real input, a written answer and its sources.

items.name: hero-18
items.title: Hero 18 – Sunlit water hero with forecast panel
items.description: A full-bleed centered hero over caustics: a net of sunlight drifts and folds as if through slow, shallow water, gathering low in the frame and held to a dim, greyed glint in dark mode. The pointer is a finger on the surface: the net bends round it like a lens and settles on a spring. The headline, copy and two actions sit above a wide forecast panel with three totals and an hourly bar chart. Pale blue over warm sand in light mode, deep blue in dark mode.

items.name: hero-19
items.title: Hero 19 – Centered hero with live feed over frosted-glass dots
items.description: A full-bleed centered hero over a dot grid seen through frosted glass: every dot is spread into a soft bloom that runs into its neighbours, slow waves swell them, a faint sheen lies across the pane and fine grain covers it. The pointer lifts the blooms round it a little, and the glass fades out behind the copy. In dark mode the blooms stay close to the page with only a hint of the chart colour. Below the headline and two actions sits the product, a live event feed card with status badges. Best for data, analytics and real-time products.

items.name: hero-20
items.title: Hero 20 – Split hero with code review card over stepped glass slats
items.description: A full-bleed split hero on the muted colour, over slats: one large, soft disc of ink seen through three full-height panels of glass with hard edges. Each panel shows its own copy of the disc, the same size and on the same line, with the dense core hard against the panel's leading edge and the ink thinning evenly to a soft round rim, so each copy is cut off mid-colour by the next: three crisp steps. The copies slide sideways behind the glass at their own pace, never up or down, and heavy, even paper grain covers the whole sheet. The pointer draws the copies gently toward it. By day each is a vivid disc with a near-black core; in dark mode it glows, brightest at the core. The headline, copy and two actions sit on the left, and the product, a finished code review with three findings, sits low on the right. On small screens the slats show in a band between the copy and the card.

items.name: hero-21
items.title: Hero 21 – Left-aligned hero with launch timeline beside a ribbon behind frosted glass
items.description: A full-bleed hero beside ribbon: a ribbon of frosted glass falls down the open right side of the frame in a slow S that travels along it. One edge stays sharp and the other dissolves into grain as the focus moves down it, with a fold of light along its middle. A pane of frosted glass with a hard top edge covers the lower half, and behind it the same ribbon is a wide, grainy blur. The pointer bends the ribbon toward it and pulls that stretch into focus. The ribbon is turned from the chart colour and fades out under the navigation bar. The headline, copy and two actions sit top left, and the product, a launch timeline with four tasks, rises from the bottom edge beneath them, leaving the ribbon in full view. On small screens the ribbon shows between the copy and the timeline.

items.name: hero-22
items.title: Hero 22 – Split hero with wind-down card under a half-disc behind fluted glass
items.description: A full-bleed split hero over melt: a flat, pure red half-disc on heavily grained paper. Below its straight cut the sheet is fluted glass: each upright rib is a rounded lens that gathers the lower half of the disc into its own soft streak, lit along one flank and gently shaded on the other. The glass has no outline, so the streaks pale toward its sides and fade into the paper. They only move up and down, and the pointer draws the ones beneath it a little further. The colour is the chart hue turned to red; in dark mode the paper is dark and keeps its grain. The headline, copy and two actions sit bottom left, and the product, an evening wind-down card with progress and four steps, sits under the disc on the right with the streaks falling behind it. On small screens the disc shows between the copy and the card.

items.name: hero-23
items.title: Hero 23 – Split hero with savings pots card over stepped pastel bands
items.description: A full-bleed hero over bands: one smooth pastel wash running down the page, from cyan through lilac and pink to a pale blush ground, cut into upright bands of two widths. Each band shows the wash a little higher or lower, so the edges read as clean steps. There is almost no grain. Every band rises and falls at its own pace and the pointer lifts the ones near it. The colours are the chart hue turned round the wheel; in dark mode the same hues glow over a deep plum ground. The headline, copy and two actions sit on the left and the product, a card of savings pots with progress, on the right. Best for finance, wellbeing and consumer apps.

items.name: hero-24
items.title: Hero 24 – Centred hero with home energy card inside a ring of soft orbs
items.description: A full-bleed centred hero over orbs: several large, very soft orbs in green, mint and cyan, each with one firmer edge, set round a clear centre on a pale, finely grained field. The orbs sway round the centre and breathe, and the pointer draws the nearest one a little closer. In dark mode they glow round a centre that stays dark. The headline, copy and two actions sit in the clear centre, with the product, a home energy card with three figures and a schedule, beneath them. Best for climate, health and calm consumer products.

items.name: hero-25
items.title: Hero 25 – Split hero with guest list card over grainy overlapping petals
items.description: A full-bleed hero over petals: a fan of large overlapping petals in coral and pink opening from one root low in the frame. Each petal has one firmer edge, dissolves into grain along the other and lets the one beneath show faintly through. A lilac haze and a warm cream glow lie along the bottom, all under visible grain. The fan slowly opens and turns and the pointer opens the nearest petal. In dark mode the petals glow on a deep wine ground. The headline, copy and two actions sit top left on the clear page, and the product, an invitation's guest list with replies, sits bottom right over the petals. Best for events, lifestyle and beauty brands.

items.name: hero-26
items.title: Hero 26 – Oversized headline with quote and logos over a warm mesh wash
items.description: A full-bleed, left-aligned hero over mesh: wide pools of warm paper, apricot and pale gold that drift and merge across the whole page, sprayed into fine stipple where they meet, with soft creases and grain. One pool follows the pointer and brightens under it. In dark mode the pools glow like embers on a deep umber ground. A huge headline reveals word by word above a rule; beneath it sit two columns, the supporting line with two actions and a customer quote with a profile card, then a strip of customer logos. The navigation bar is see-through from medium screens up. Best for finance, operations and B2B products that lead with a claim and proof.

meta.containerClassName: h-svh

meta.containerClassName: h-svh

items.docs: `lib/demo-threads.ts` is the file to delete. Implement `ThreadStore`'s four methods against your own backend, pass the result as `store`, and the optimistic updates in `lib/threads-store.tsx` keep working unchanged.

It holds its open state itself rather than borrowing a SidebarProvider, so the sidebar your app already has keeps its trigger, its shortcut and its collapse. It brings a whole working chat with it, so what your app supplies is the page it sits beside.

meta.containerClassName: h-svh

items.docs: The panel needs nothing from your `SidebarProvider`: it holds its open state in `components/assistant-provider.tsx` and answers to ⌘J, so your own sidebar keeps its trigger, ⌘B and its collapse. Mount `AssistantProvider` above your page, put the panel beside it, and `AssistantTrigger` in your own header. Rename and delete are built in, IME guards and focus handling included, and land in `onRename` and `onDelete`: `index.tsx` implements both against the demo array, and pointing them at your backend is the whole integration. `index.tsx`, `components/site-sidebar.tsx` and `lib/demo-sessions.ts` are the stand-ins to replace, and `components/assistant-panel.tsx` is the panel. The conversation inside it is `chat-1`, mounted unchanged, so the transport and the message renderers are documented there rather than here.

items.name: chat-1

items.docs: `lib/demo-chat.ts` is the file to delete: point the transport at your own route, then drop `@shadcn/helpers`. items.name: share-dialog-1
items.title: Share Dialog 1 – Scoped link for a conversation
items.description: Publishes a conversation to a link. Picking who can see it is the act of sharing, so there is no second confirm button and the link is one click from the clipboard. Opens from the control you already render, a header button or a row in a thread menu. Works with no backend behind it, and takes a real one when you have it.

meta.containerClassName: px-5 py-12 lg:px-8 lg:py-20 preview-wrapper

items.docs: Pass `open` and `onOpenChange` from wherever the button lives, and a `key` of the thread id so sharing one thread and then another does not carry the first thread's link across. `ShareDialog1Demo` is the preview wiring, there to be deleted.

items.name: composer-1
items.title: Composer 1 – Prompt input with attachments, model and dictation
items.description: The prompt input, and the hardest part of a chat to get right. Files arrive by picker, drag or paste, each reporting its own upload state; a menu switches tools and connectors on for the turn; the model picker carries reasoning effort with it; and dictation swaps the field for a live waveform without shifting the layout. The unsent draft survives leaving and coming back. Speaks the AI SDK's message shape, and drops into a chat you already have.

meta.containerClassName: min-h-svh content-end mx-auto max-w-3xl px-5 pb-12 lg:px-8 lg:pb-20

items.docs: `onSubmit` is the seam: it hands you the text and the files, and nothing else. What the model picker, the tool switches and the connectors are set to is a preference rather than part of the message, so it is held in `localStorage` and survives a reload without passing through your submit handler. Drafts are kept the same way, one per `draftKey`. Dictation runs on the browser's own Web Speech API, which asks for the microphone on first use. The button stays visible where that API is missing, since support cannot be read before the first attempt: pressing it reports the refusal through `onError`, which this block sends to a toast.

items.name: assistant-onboarding-1
items.title: Assistant Onboarding 1 – Chat-style setup for an AI assistant
items.description: Onboarding that reads as a conversation, not a form wizard: the assistant asks for its name, role, tools and tone one turn at a time, answered with quick replies, switches, sample replies or a typed line. Earlier answers stay editable, a step count tracks progress, and a summary card ends in Start chatting. Scripted, so it needs no model.

meta.containerClassName: h-svh

items.docs: `lib/setup.ts` is the script: the questions, their order and the answers on offer. `components/setup-parts.tsx` holds the flow and the control each step answers with, `components/thread.tsx` the turns and the answer field, and `index.tsx` is only the layout. `onStart` receives the finished answers, which is where you save them and route to your chat. Pass `defaultAnswers` to resume a setup that was left part-way.

items.name: assistant-onboarding-2
items.title: Assistant Onboarding 2 – Chat-style setup beside a live profile card
items.description: The assistant-onboarding-1 conversation in a split layout: questions and answers on the left, and on the right a profile card that fills in with the assistant's name, role, tools and tone as each answer lands. The card carries Start chatting, enabled once nothing is missing. On small screens it folds to a strip above the chat.

meta.containerClassName: h-svh

items.docs: The flow, turns and controls come from `assistant-onboarding-1` (`lib/setup.ts` and `components/setup-parts.tsx`); this block adds the split layout and the profile card. `onStart` receives the finished answers.

items.name: assistant-onboarding-3
items.title: Assistant Onboarding 3 – Connect knowledge sources in a setup chat
items.description: The setup step where an AI assistant is given something to read, as a turn in a chat. The assistant asks, and a card under its message connects Notion, Dropbox, Zendesk or Slack, or uploads files, then shows each source indexing page by page with a reconnect action on any that fail. A website is added by pasting its address into the message field. Ships loading, empty and error states, and Continue unlocks once one source is ready.

meta.containerClassName: h-svh

items.docs: Two timers stand in for your backend: one for the fetch of connected sources, one that advances sources still indexing. Swap the first for your query and the second for a poll or subscription to your indexer. `handleSend` is where a typed address becomes a source. `initialStatus` and `initialSources` set what the block opens with, `step` and `totalSteps` set the header, and `onContinue` receives the sources. `components/thread.tsx` is the chat around the step.

items.name: assistant-onboarding-4
items.title: Assistant Onboarding 4 – Permissions in a setup chat, with a live exchange
items.description: The setup step that sets how far an AI assistant may go on its own, as a turn in a chat. A card under the assistant's message sets each action, from answering to refunds to deleting data, to never, ask first or allowed, and its next message plays the last action touched as a real exchange: the customer's message, the approval request sent to the team, and the assistant's reply. Typing a level sets every action at once.

meta.containerClassName: h-svh

items.docs: `PERMISSIONS` is the list to replace: each action carries its default level and the reply shown at every level. Nothing is fetched. `step` and `totalSteps` set the header, and `onSave` receives the level chosen for each action id. `components/thread.tsx` is the chat around the step.

items.name: assistant-onboarding-5
items.title: Assistant Onboarding 5 – Teach the assistant your voice by example, in a chat
items.description: Tone training for an AI assistant, done by example inside a setup chat. A card under the assistant's message shows its draft reply to a real customer message; each draft is kept or sent back as too formal, too long or too cheerful, or with a reason typed into the message field, and every decision joins a list of what it has learned. The card holds one height across samples, and the last turn is a Voice saved summary with Start chatting.

meta.containerClassName: h-svh

items.docs: `SAMPLES` holds the scripted drafts and `REASONS` the ways one can be rejected. With a model behind it, regenerate the next draft from the rules learned so far. `defaultDecisions` resumes part-way through, `step` and `totalSteps` set the header, and `onFinish` receives the learned rules. `components/thread.tsx` is the chat around the step.

items.name: assistant-onboarding-6
items.title: Assistant Onboarding 6 – Choose a model in a setup chat, with trade-off meters
items.description: The setup step that picks the model behind an AI assistant, as a turn in a chat. A card under the assistant's message holds three radio cards with segmented ten-step meters for speed, reasoning and cost, and a volume slider that turns the choice into a monthly estimate. The assistant's next message answers one customer question the way the chosen model would, with time to first word and cost per reply.

meta.containerClassName: h-svh

items.docs: `MODELS` is the list to replace: each model carries its meter values, latency, cost per reply and sample answer. Nothing is fetched. `step` and `totalSteps` set the header, and `onContinue` receives the model id and the monthly conversation volume. `components/thread.tsx` is the chat around the step.

items.name: assistant-onboarding-7
items.title: Assistant Onboarding 7 – Connect tools in a setup chat, with a switch per tool
items.description: MCP-style tool setup for an AI assistant, as a turn in a chat. A card under the assistant's message lists apps with their real logos; connecting one opens its tools, each with its own switch and a mark for read only or makes changes. Any other server is added by pasting its URL into the message field. Ships loading, empty and error states for the app list, and the card's footer counts connected apps and tools switched on.

meta.containerClassName: h-svh

items.docs: A timer stands in for the fetch of the servers on offer; swap it for your query. `SERVERS` is the list to replace, and `handleSend` is where a typed URL becomes a server. `initialStatus` and `initialServers` set what the block opens with, `step` and `totalSteps` set the header, and `onContinue` receives every server with its tool switches. `components/thread.tsx` is the chat around the step.

items.name: assistant-onboarding-8
items.title: Assistant Onboarding 8 – Set up memory in a chat, with editable memory chips
items.description: Memory setup for an AI assistant, as a turn in a chat. A card under the assistant's message has one switch for memory and a row of chips for what it already knows: press one to reword it in place, remove it, or type a new one into the message field. The assistant's next message writes the same reply with and without those memories and counts the ones it used, so the effect is seen rather than described.

meta.containerClassName: h-svh

items.docs: `MEMORIES` is the list to replace; a memory's optional `effect` is what it adds to the sample reply in the preview. Nothing is fetched. `step` and `totalSteps` set the header, and `onContinue` receives the switch and the memories. `components/thread.tsx` is the chat around the step.

items.name: assistant-onboarding-9
items.title: Assistant Onboarding 9 – Persona builder in a chat, with a live avatar and greeting
items.description: The setup step that gives an AI assistant a face and a manner, as a turn in a chat. Fill, shape and symbol tiles combine into a generated avatar built from the theme's chart colors, Shuffle rolls a new one, and two sliders set warmth and detail. The avatar beside every message in the thread is the one being built, and the assistant's next message is its greeting, rewritten live to match. A name is typed into the message field.

meta.containerClassName: h-svh

items.docs: `FILLS`, `SHAPES` and `GLYPHS` are the avatar's parts, and `OPENERS` and `FOLLOW_UPS` the greeting at each slider stop. Nothing is fetched. `step` and `totalSteps` set the header, and `onContinue` receives the persona. `components/thread.tsx` is the chat around the step.

items.name: assistant-onboarding-10
items.title: Assistant Onboarding 10 – Pick a voice in a setup chat, with playable samples
items.description: Voice selection for an AI assistant, as a turn in a chat. A card under the assistant's message lists each voice as a row with its own waveform and a play button that runs the sample through the bars, one voice at a time, with the time left counting down; a radio on the row chooses it and a slider sets the speaking pace. Typing a voice's name chooses it too.

meta.containerClassName: h-svh

items.docs: `VOICES` is the list to replace, with each `wave` set to the sample's real peaks. A timer stands in for playback: start and stop your audio element in `toggle` and drive `progress` from `timeupdate`. `step` and `totalSteps` set the header, and `onContinue` receives the voice id and the pace. `components/thread.tsx` is the chat around the step.

items.name: assistant-onboarding-11
items.title: Assistant Onboarding 11 – Privacy controls in a chat, with a live redaction preview
items.description: Privacy setup for an AI assistant, as a turn in a chat. A card under the assistant's message sets how long conversations are kept, which personal details are hidden before storage, and whether conversations may train the model. The assistant's next message shows one real customer message as it will be saved, blacking out each address, phone number, email or card as its switch goes on. Opens on the most private choices.

meta.containerClassName: h-svh

items.docs: `RETENTION`, `DETAILS` and `SAMPLE` are the lists to replace; `SAMPLE` is one message split so each personal detail can be hidden on its own. Nothing is fetched. `step` and `totalSteps` set the header, and `onContinue` receives the settings. `components/thread.tsx` is the chat around the step.

items.name: assistant-onboarding-12
items.title: Assistant Onboarding 12 – Starter prompt gallery in a chat, with a new-chat preview
items.description: Starter prompts for an AI assistant, chosen as a turn in a chat. A card under the assistant's message holds a gallery of templates, filtered by kind and pinned by pressing them, up to four; a prompt of your own is added by typing it into the message field. The assistant's next message pictures the empty chat people will open, with the pinned prompts as its suggestion chips above the message box. Ships loading, empty and error states for the gallery.

meta.containerClassName: h-svh

items.docs: A timer stands in for the fetch of the templates; swap it for your query. `TEMPLATES` is the list to replace, and `handleSend` is where a typed prompt joins it. `initialStatus`, `initialTemplates` and `defaultPinned` set what the block opens with, `step` and `totalSteps` set the header, and `onContinue` receives the pinned templates. `components/thread.tsx` is the chat around the step.
